body.p: This project investigates the historical and conceptual entanglement of atheistic thought across multiple national contexts. It brings together textual fragments, editorial metadata, and keyword annotations to trace how ideas concerning materialism, naturalism, secular humanism, and religious critique circulate through nineteenth-century discourse. Rather than treating atheism as a single, stable doctrine, the corpus is organized to reveal its heterogeneous patterns of emergence, adaptation, and debate. The resulting dataset is designed as a heuristic instrument for scholarly comparison: a structured archive of language, argument, and context, assembled to support analysis of how secular reason and anti-theological claims are historically embedded in social and intellectual networks.
